hunks.baseline: I squeezed out every last ounce of strength and activated my movement technique. Each time the scenery flashed past, the ruined city drew closer at terrifying speed.
hunks.sol: I squeezed out every last ounce of strength and pushed my movement technique to its limit. The scenery blurred past as the ruined city rapidly drew closer.

hunks.baseline: But I could tell how things had ended before I even arrived. No—I should say someone had told me.
hunks.sol: But I knew how it had ended before I even arrived. No—I should say someone told me.

hunks.baseline: The moment I heard the System notification, the tension that had been wound tight inside me abruptly released.
hunks.sol: The moment I heard the System notification, the tension wound tight inside me abruptly snapped.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t because I had failed the Quest, nor because my stat had decreased. I knew what this meant.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t because I had failed the Quest or because my stat had decreased. It was because I knew what the notification meant.

hunks.baseline: The silence I felt as I drew closer to the city, followed by the scene that unfolded before my eyes moments later, changed my suspicion into certainty.
hunks.sol: The deepening silence as I approached the city—and the sight that greeted me moments later—turned my suspicion into certainty.

hunks.baseline: Blood covered the area in every direction, and corpses lay scattered in horrifying positions. Even I, who had grown accustomed to death after fighting countless battles, froze for a moment.
hunks.sol: Blood was everywhere, and horribly mangled corpses lay strewn across the ground. Even I, after countless battles had made me accustomed to death, froze for a moment.

hunks.baseline: *Massacre.*
hunks.sol: *Slaughter.*

hunks.baseline: Yes. This was a massacre. They had blown people apart, torn them to pieces, and crushed them.
hunks.sol: Yes. This was slaughter. They had blown people apart, torn them to pieces, and crushed them.

hunks.baseline: The sight of living humans having been hunted down and killed like ants made it hard to breathe.
hunks.sol: The evidence that living human beings had been hunted down and killed like ants made it hard to breathe.

hunks.baseline: If even I, an outsider from another country who had never met these people, felt that way, then the grief and rage of the Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department who arrived behind me could not be expressed in words.
hunks.sol: If even I, a complete stranger from another country, felt this way, the grief and rage of the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters arriving behind me were beyond words.

hunks.baseline: These were the comrades who had entrusted each other with their backs. Among the people lying there as cold corpses were their brothers and their lovers.
hunks.sol: These were comrades who had entrusted their backs to one another. Among the cold bodies lying before them were their siblings and lovers.

hunks.baseline: Amid the endless wailing and shouting, one person who had been standing silently suddenly took a step forward.
hunks.sol: Amid the endless wailing and shouting, one person who had been standing in silence suddenly stepped forward.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps his hollow footsteps sounded especially loud because, unlike his usual self, his face was utterly numb and devoid of emotion.
hunks.sol: Perhaps his hollow footsteps sounded especially loud because his face, so unlike its usual self, was utterly numb and devoid of emotion.

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi, standing beside me, called my name in a low voice.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi, standing beside me, called my name quietly.

hunks.baseline: Sometimes there were things you had to do even when you didn’t want to. This was one of those times, and I painfully forced my lips apart.
hunks.sol: Some things had to be done even when you wanted no part of them. This was one of those times. I forced the words past my lips.

hunks.baseline: Despite my forceful shout, Shao Shen’s footsteps did not stop. He simply continued walking toward some unknown place in search of the criminals who had killed his subordinates.
hunks.sol: Even my forceful shout failed to stop him. Shao Shen merely kept walking toward some unknown place, searching for the killers who had murdered his subordinates.

hunks.baseline: In the end, I had to approach him myself and grab his shoulder.
hunks.sol: In the end, I had to walk up and grab him by the shoulder.

hunks.baseline: A dry, lifeless voice spilled out.
hunks.sol: A dry, lifeless voice emerged.

hunks.baseline: 「I have to chase them. I’ll find them somehow, no matter what it takes, and I’ll have my revenge.」
hunks.sol: 「I have to go after them. No matter what it takes, I’ll find them and have my revenge.」

hunks.baseline: For a moment, I was unable to speak.
hunks.sol: For a moment, I couldn’t speak.

hunks.baseline: The man I saw before me was not Shao Shen. He was me, a few years ago.
hunks.sol: The person before me wasn’t Shao Shen. He was me, a few years ago.

hunks.baseline: That was why I couldn’t easily say what needed to be said.
hunks.sol: That was why I couldn’t bring myself to say what needed to be said.

hunks.baseline: He wanted to kill them, and he probably wanted to die as well.
hunks.sol: He wanted to kill, and he probably wanted to die too.

hunks.baseline: The feelings left behind by the deaths of those close to you weren’t only rage and grief. For the survivor, there was guilt waiting—heavier than those two emotions combined.
hunks.sol: The deaths of those close to you left behind more than rage and grief. The survivor was burdened with guilt heavier than both combined.

hunks.baseline: The guilt left behind by a hundred deaths was far too heavy for a twenty-one-year-old young man to bear.
hunks.sol: The guilt left behind by a hundred lives was far too much for a twenty-one-year-old to bear.

hunks.baseline: I swallowed the curse circling the tip of my tongue and tightened my grip on his shoulder.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the curse lingering on the tip of my tongue and tightened my grip on his shoulder.

hunks.baseline: “It’s already too late. We can’t find them right now. This isn’t a guess. I know it for certain.”
hunks.sol: “It’s already too late. We can’t find them right now. That isn’t a guess. I’m certain.”

hunks.baseline: The System notification had told me so. There was no way I could be wrong.
hunks.sol: The System notification had told me as much. There was no possibility of a mistake.

hunks.baseline: Shao Shen met my confident gaze and muttered blankly.
hunks.sol: Shao Shen stared into my unwavering eyes and murmured blankly.

hunks.baseline: 「I’m too late. It really is too late.」
hunks.sol: 「I’m too late. I really am too late.」

hunks.baseline: “I don’t want to admit it either, but… yes. That’s reality.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t want to admit it either, but… yes. That’s the reality.”

hunks.baseline: I thought he would finally let his suppressed rage and grief erupt.
hunks.sol: I thought he would finally unleash all the rage and grief he had been holding back.

hunks.baseline: Just as I had done years ago, I thought he would cry out loud and smash anything he could see.
hunks.sol: I thought he would wail and smash everything in sight, just as I had a few years ago.

hunks.baseline: But I was wrong. The object of Shao Shen’s desire for revenge wasn’t limited to the monsters.
hunks.sol: But I was wrong. The monsters weren’t the only targets of Shao Shen’s revenge.

hunks.baseline: As Shao Shen watched the advancing column draw closer from a distant speck, his eyes burned like flames.
hunks.sol: Shao Shen watched the advancing column grow from distant specks into looming vehicles, his eyes blazing like fire.

hunks.baseline: 「Then I suppose I’ll have to kill that bastard, at least.」
hunks.sol: 「Then I’ll have to kill that bastard instead.」

hunks.baseline: It was obvious who *that bastard* referred to.
hunks.sol: There was no question who *that bastard* meant.

hunks.baseline: Because of a single ridiculous order from that bastard, a hundred Hunters and hundreds of soldiers had died. Even I thought he was someone who absolutely had to pay the price.
hunks.sol: One worthless command from him had killed a hundred Hunters and hundreds of soldiers. Even I thought he deserved to pay for it.

hunks.baseline: Shao Shen sensed something was wrong and tried to evade me, but my hand moved fluidly and had already brushed his acupoints.
hunks.sol: Shao Shen sensed something was wrong and tried to dodge, but my hand moved like flowing water and brushed his acupoints before he could escape.

hunks.baseline: Shao Shen’s entire body went rigid, his voice was cut off, and deep sleep began to overtake him.
hunks.sol: Shao Shen’s entire body went rigid, his voice was sealed, and a deep sleep began to overtake him.

hunks.baseline: His eyelids trembled as though he were struggling with all his strength to resist the drowsiness pouring over him.
hunks.sol: His eyelids trembled as he fought desperately against the drowsiness pouring over him.

hunks.baseline: In the end, his eyelids closed firmly. The last thing I saw in Shao Shen’s eyes was unmistakable confusion.
hunks.sol: At last, his eyelids closed tight. The final look in Shao Shen’s eyes held an unmistakable question.

hunks.baseline: *Why? How come?*
hunks.sol: *Why? Why are you doing this?*

hunks.baseline: And Shao Shen wasn’t the only one who felt that way.
hunks.sol: And Shao Shen wasn’t the only one asking it.

hunks.baseline: Along with furious shouts, five sounds of air being split apart rang out.
hunks.sol: Five streaks tore through the air amid furious shouts.

hunks.baseline: They were A-rank Hunters under Shao Shen’s command, men called company commanders.
hunks.sol: They came from the A-rank Hunters serving beneath Shao Shen—the men they called company commanders.

hunks.baseline: With the sound of compressed air exploding outward, the weapons flying at me abruptly changed direction.
hunks.sol: Compressed air exploded outward, forcing the weapons hurtling toward me to veer away.

hunks.baseline: The company commanders barely blocked the palm force that had torn through the air toward them, and their bodies slid backward across the ground.
hunks.sol: The company commanders barely managed to block the palm force tearing through the air, their bodies skidding backward across the ground.

hunks.baseline: It was fortunate that I had restrained my strength. If I had truly steeled myself, things would not have ended this easily.
hunks.sol: They were lucky I had held back. If I had truly meant to hurt them, it wouldn’t have ended there.

hunks.baseline: As the atmosphere grew more hostile, Team Leader Choi stepped forward and spoke in a low voice.
hunks.sol: As the atmosphere turned hostile, Team Leader Choi stepped forward and spoke quietly.

hunks.baseline: “Mr. Jin is only repaying the favor.”
hunks.sol: “Mr. Jin is only repaying that kindness.”

hunks.baseline: “If we had left him alone, the enraged Regimental Commander Shao would have killed General Liao.”
hunks.sol: “If he had done nothing, the enraged Regimental Commander Shao would have killed General Liao.”

hunks.baseline: “I agree. But I don’t know what your country’s Central Committee would think of that—especially the Crown Prince Party, which General Liao belongs to.”
hunks.sol: “I agree. But I can’t say how your country’s Central Committee would view it—especially the Crown Prince Party, to which General Liao belongs.”

hunks.baseline: “The man you’re talking about is the supreme commander responsible for an entire front. If you kill him, it won’t end as a personal matter.”
hunks.sol: “He is the supreme commander responsible for an entire front. Killing him would not remain a personal matter.”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi looked over the Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department one by one.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi looked over the Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters one by one.

hunks.baseline: They were a force numbering around a thousand. I hadn’t thought that far ahead, but if they became involved in an incident like this, they wouldn’t be able to avoid trouble either.
hunks.sol: They were a force nearly a thousand strong. I hadn’t thought that far ahead, but if they became entangled in an incident like this, they wouldn’t escape the consequences either.

hunks.baseline: “I’m not telling you to forget what happened today. I’m only saying that now isn’t the time.”
hunks.sol: “I won’t tell you to forget what happened today. I’m only saying that now is not the time.”

hunks.baseline: I could feel the hostile atmosphere beginning to settle.
hunks.sol: I felt the hostility begin to subside.

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi’s words were both practical and grounded in emotion. One of the company commanders who had not joined the attack finally spoke.
hunks.sol: His words appealed to both reason and emotion. One of the company commanders who hadn’t joined the attack finally spoke.

hunks.baseline: 「I agree. Dealing with that bastard right now would be easy, but… if we did, it would be difficult to deal with the consequences.」
hunks.sol: 「I agree. Killing that bastard right now would be easy, but… dealing with the aftermath would not.」

hunks.baseline: 「Remember this. Our brothers didn’t die solely because of General Liao.」
hunks.sol: 「Remember this. General Liao isn’t the only reason our brothers died.」

hunks.baseline: After looking around at the horrific sea of corpses and blood, he ground his teeth.
hunks.sol: He surveyed the horrific sea of corpses and blood, then ground his teeth.

hunks.baseline: 「Let’s wait a little. Just a little longer. The time will come soon.」
hunks.sol: 「Let’s wait. Just a little while. Our time will come soon.」

hunks.baseline: Some people looked up at the sky and lamented. Others failed to contain the grief and rage surging inside them.
hunks.sol: Some looked to the sky and lamented. Others struggled to contain the grief and fury boiling inside them.

hunks.baseline: But it was clear that they had all reached the same tacit agreement.
hunks.sol: But it was clear that they had all reached the same unspoken agreement.

hunks.baseline: Once the situation finally came to an end, Team Leader Choi let out a relieved sigh.
hunks.sol: Once the situation had finally settled, Team Leader Choi let out a relieved sigh.

hunks.baseline: “We can finally breathe. It’s fortunate that you stopped Regimental Commander Shao, Mr. Jin.”
hunks.sol: “That’s one less thing to worry about. I’m glad you stopped Regimental Commander Shao, Mr. Jin.”

hunks.baseline: Fortunate. Was this really something we should call fortunate?
hunks.sol: Glad. Could anything about this really be called fortunate?

hunks.baseline: Even knowing that there had been no other choice, I was left with a bitter taste in my mouth. I knew the rage and grief Shao Shen must have felt.
hunks.sol: Even though I knew there had been no other choice, a bitter taste lingered in my mouth. I knew the rage and grief Shao Shen must have felt.

hunks.baseline: “More importantly, it seemed there were survivors.”
hunks.sol: “More importantly, I heard there were survivors.”

hunks.baseline: “There was a middle-aged couple and one child. They apparently fainted from extreme tension, so they’re being moved somewhere else to rest for now.”
hunks.sol: “They found a middle-aged couple and a child. All three apparently fainted from the extreme strain, so they’re being moved elsewhere to rest for now.”

hunks.baseline: “We’ll find them soon enough.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll find out soon enough.”

hunks.baseline: “Once the order comes down from that utterly incompetent commander, at least.”
hunks.sol: “Once that utterly incompetent commander gives the order, at least.”

hunks.baseline: The armored vehicle advancing with a deafening racket stopped about twenty meters ahead of us.
hunks.sol: The armored vehicle advancing with a deafening racket stopped about twenty meters away.

hunks.baseline: A moment later, under heavy escort, the plump General Liao emerged.
hunks.sol: A moment later, the plump General Liao emerged under heavy guard.

hunks.baseline: At the horrific sight before him, his already fair complexion turned deathly pale.
hunks.sol: At the horrific sight before him, his already pale complexion turned deathly white.

hunks.baseline: Watching him bend over and retch for quite some time, I felt disgusted—but I also found myself thinking that he was human after all.
hunks.sol: He doubled over and retched for a long while. The sight filled me with disgust, but it also made me think that perhaps he was human after all.

hunks.baseline: *You bastard. I guess you do feel some guilt.*
hunks.sol: *You bastard. I guess you do feel guilty.*

hunks.baseline: Everyone here had probably been thinking the same thing as me.
hunks.sol: Everyone there had probably thought the same thing.

hunks.baseline: But the next words General Liao spoke reminded me of a lesson I had forgotten.
hunks.sol: But General Liao’s next words reminded me of something I had forgotten.

hunks.baseline: People like him always exceeded the limits of imagination.
hunks.sol: People like him always managed to exceed the limits of imagination.

hunks.baseline: 「N-No. The operation wasn’t supposed to fail!」
hunks.sol: 「N-No. This operation couldn’t fail!」

hunks.baseline: Like a slow-motion scene, I saw shock and rage rise across the faces of the people around me.
hunks.sol: As though in slow motion, I saw shock and fury spread across the faces around me.

hunks.baseline: I saw Team Leader Choi reaching out toward me and shouting urgently.
hunks.sol: I saw Team Leader Choi reach for me and heard his urgent shout.

hunks.baseline: By the time he called my name, I had already crossed the twenty-odd meters and arrived in front of General Liao.
hunks.sol: By the time he called my name, I had crossed the twenty-odd meters between us and appeared before General Liao.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t hold back a laugh.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t suppress the incredulous laugh that escaped me.

hunks.baseline: I reached out toward the man staring up at me with a blank face, as though he were looking at a ghost.
hunks.sol: I reached toward the man staring up at me as though he had seen a ghost.

hunks.baseline: It happened in an instant.
hunks.sol: It was over in an instant.

hunks.baseline: Using nothing but physical strength, without a single thread of internal energy, I broke both his arms and crushed his kneecaps.
hunks.sol: With pure physical strength, without putting so much as a thread of internal energy behind it, I broke both his arms and crushed his kneecaps.

hunks.baseline: *Consider yourself lucky I still have a shred of reason left.*
hunks.sol: *Be grateful I still have one shred of reason left.*

hunks.baseline: His mouth hung open. His eyes bulged wide.
hunks.sol: His jaw dropped. His eyes bulged.

hunks.baseline: Then a scream like a pig being slaughtered burst from him.
hunks.sol: Then he screamed like a pig being slaughtered.

hunks.baseline: I spat at him as he rolled his eyes back, collapsed to the ground, and convulsed in pain, then turned away.
hunks.sol: His eyes rolled back as he collapsed and convulsed in pain. I spat on him and turned away.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t forget to say one thing to the staff officer staring at me with a face drained of all spirit.
hunks.sol: I didn’t forget to address the staff officer staring at me as though his soul had left his body.

hunks.baseline: “Report it to your superiors if you’ve got a fucking problem, you bastards.”
hunks.sol: “Report me to your superiors if you’ve got a fucking problem, you bastards.”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi shook his head repeatedly and approached with a high-grade potion.
hunks.sol: Shaking his head, Team Leader Choi approached with a high-grade potion.

hunks.baseline: The chair was enormous and bizarre.
hunks.sol: The chair was enormous and grotesque.

hunks.baseline: That was only natural. It had been made from human and monster bones.
hunks.sol: That was only natural. It had been fashioned from human and monster bones.

hunks.baseline: But it was not as bizarre or terrifying as its owner.
hunks.sol: Yet it was neither as grotesque nor as terrifying as its owner.

hunks.baseline: A finger without a trace of flesh tapped the skull decorating the armrest.
hunks.sol: A fleshless finger tapped the skull decorating the armrest.

hunks.baseline: The figure stood well over three meters tall, with an enormous frame. A black robe draped over it rippled like mist.
hunks.sol: The figure was well over three meters tall, with a massive frame. The black robe draped over it rippled like mist.

hunks.baseline: It looked like a king seated upon a throne, and that wasn’t entirely wrong.
hunks.sol: It resembled a king seated upon a throne, and that description was not far from the truth.

hunks.baseline: It was an existence worthy of being called the lord of the undead and the king who ruled over death.
hunks.sol: It was a being worthy of being called the lord of the undead—a king who ruled over death.

hunks.baseline: But the Arch Lich itself did not think that way. There was a true king elsewhere, and it was merely his loyal servant.
hunks.sol: But the Arch Lich itself did not think so. There was another who was the true king, while it was merely that king’s loyal servant.

hunks.baseline: The Arch Lich suddenly felt a pang of regret.
hunks.sol: The Arch Lich felt a sudden pang of regret.

hunks.baseline: It possessed truly formidable magical power, but it was still far weaker than the strength it had once possessed. On top of that, the situation on the battlefield was proving more difficult than expected.
hunks.sol: It possessed immense magical power, but that power still fell far short of what it had once commanded. Worse, the war was proving more difficult than expected.

hunks.baseline: After silently sinking into thought, the Arch Lich opened its mouth.
hunks.sol: After a long silence, the Arch Lich spoke.

hunks.baseline: The being kneeling in the darkness answered.
hunks.sol: The being prostrated in the darkness answered.

hunks.baseline: “Pull back the front line. We’ll draw the human army in.”
hunks.sol: “Pull back the front line. Draw the human army in.”

hunks.baseline: “Go. Deliver my command to every legion within the reach of my power.”
hunks.sol: “Go. Carry my command to every legion within the reach of my power.”

hunks.baseline: The black knight rose and slowly backed away.
hunks.sol: The black knight rose and slowly withdrew.

hunks.baseline: At the final moment, the Arch Lich’s chair was reflected in his eyes, which burned red.
hunks.sol: Just before he vanished, his burning red gaze caught the chair upon which the Arch Lich sat.

hunks.baseline: The skull decorating the armrest was far too small to have belonged to an adult.
hunks.sol: The skull decorating its armrest was far too small to have belonged to an adult.
